title: Unified Static-Dynamic Pruning for Efficient LLM Inference
event_hint: PVLDB 2026 paper (Seoul National University, arXiv:2607.21985v1) introduces SPDP, a unified static+dynamic weight-pruning GPU kernel framework for LLM decode/prefill inference.
problem: LLM autoregressive decoding is memory-/bandwidth-bound, and existing weight-pruning systems are either purely static (fixed offline patterns, no input adaptivity) or purely dynamic (coarse-grained structured masks, hardware-incompatible, cannot exploit unstructured sparsity). Static-sparse kernels are row-major SpMM-optimized while dynamic pruning induces column-wise spMspV workloads, so the two are not directly composable: naively combining them breaks memory coalescing, warp stride regularity, and Tensor Core utilization.
mechanism: SPDP co-designs a Tiled-Column-wise Bitmap Compressed (Tiled-CBC) weight layout with two kernels: (1) a CUDA-core spMspV decode kernel using Hybrid Activation-aware Dynamic Shared-Memory Bitmap Decoding (HAD-SMBD) for fine-grained runtime activation skipping, and (2) a Tensor-Core SpMM kernel for prefill that reuses the same layout via shared-memory alignment. Key insight: static pruning removes weights row-wise and dynamic pruning skips activations column-wise, acting on orthogonal dimensions, so their sparsity patterns overlap minimally and effective sparsities multiply. A roofline model (Section 3.2.3) formalizes this: CI_SPDP = M*N / (M/(CR*(1-s)) + N), where SP raises the compression ratio CR and DP cuts active columns by (1-s), so the two boost compute intensity multiplicatively in the memory-bound regime. The motivation for the co-design is the hardware-level conflict that under PTX mma.m16n8k16 a DP-induced spMspV drops Tensor-Core CI by up to 8x (achievable GEMV throughput ~one-fourth of CUDA-core FP32 peak), so a naive SP format would decode inactive fragments and fall below dense cuBLAS. The decode pipeline uses metadata-first prefetching (cp.async/LDGSTS.128, 128-bit vectors) and Split-K tiling (TILE_M=256, TILE_K=16) to hide HAD-SMBD latency; the prefill SpMM kernel adds a Layout Alignment stage for Tensor-Core execution.

evidence.claim: SPDP-spMspV kernel on A10G averages 1.24x speedup over SpInfer and 1.88x over cuBLAS (maxima 1.70x and 3.32x).
evidence.value: 1.24x avg / 1.70x max over SpInfer; 1.88x avg / 3.32x max over cuBLAS
evidence.baseline: SpInfer (SOTA Tensor-Core sparse kernel) and cuBLAS dense Tensor-Core baseline
evidence.condition: A10G GPU; static sparsity swept 0-90% with DP fixed at 30%; matrix shapes from OPT/LLaMA-2/3/Qwen/Qwen2/Mixtral/Phi/gpt-oss

evidence.claim: On L4 GPU, SPDP-spMspV averages 1.37x over SpInfer (max 2.52x) and 2.11x over cuBLAS (max 3.52x).
evidence.value: 1.37x avg / 2.52x max over SpInfer; 2.11x avg / 3.52x max over cuBLAS
evidence.condition: L4 GPU; DP fixed at 30%; same matrix-shape suite as A10G

evidence.claim: End-to-end decode TPOT speedup averages 1.34x over SpInfer at moderate sparsity on Llama-2-7B-hf while keeping perplexity under 5.4.
evidence.condition: Llama-2-7B-hf; A10G/L4/L40S; total sparsity up to 65% (best config 30% SP + 50% DP); full decode latency incl. attention/norm

evidence.claim: At matched perplexity, SPDP sustains up to 25% higher total sparsity than SpInfer (Wanda-based static pruning) with comparable or lower TPOT.
evidence.value: up to 25% higher total sparsity at matched PPL
evidence.condition: Matched perplexity (~4.97-5.34); A10G, L4, L40S GPUs

evidence.claim: SPDP-spMspV at (DP,SP)=(30%,30%) attains the highest SM-busy fraction and the lowest bank conflicts (74) versus SpInfer(30%) and SpInfer(50%) on A10G, with comparable Max bandwidth.
evidence.baseline: SpInfer at SP=30% and SP=50% (same total sparsity)
evidence.condition: A10G GPU; (DP,SP)=(30%,30%); metrics normalized to per-kernel peak

evaluation_context: Inference-optimized GPUs: A10G, L4, L40S. Kernel benchmarks use projection/FFN weight-matrix shapes from OPT(13B-175B), LLaMA-2(7B-70B), LLaMA-3(8B/70B), Qwen(7B/14B), Qwen2(7B/72B), Mixtral-8x7B MoE, Phi-2/3, gpt-oss(20B/120B). End-to-end decode run on Llama-2-7B-hf. Practical sparsity range 30-50% for both SP and DP. Baselines: cuBLAS (dense), cuSPARSE, Sputnik, SparTA, Flash-LLM, SpInfer. The roofline analysis (Section 3.2.3) treats decode as memory-bound and expresses the SP+DP gain as a compute-intensity multiplier, not a measured energy metric.
limitations: End-to-end gains are Amdahl-limited: attention, normalization and other non-sparse components are not sparsity-sensitive, and decode is memory-bound so higher sparsity improves arithmetic efficiency more than latency. Perplexity diverges sharply beyond ~70% static sparsity (Wanda impractical there). Quantization and unstructured sparsity do not compress multiplicatively in practice (low-bit reduces only Values; Bitmap, ColInfo, TileOffset and padding metadata persist). SPDP targets moderate-sparsity LLM decode; extreme-sparsity matrices (e.g., SuiteSparse) and large-N prefill (where existing works fail to beat cuBLAS) are out of scope. The targeted supplement (PDF Pages 5 and 8: roofline model, realization challenges, kernel pipeline and prefill SpMM design) provides no quantitative performance-per-watt/energy measurement and no prefill-stage Figure 12 speedup numbers, so the abstract's perf-per-watt claim and the prefill-kernel speedup remain un-located/un-quantified.
project_relevance: Falls in the serving/runtime/compiler direction: SPDP is a projection-matmul kernel replacement for LLM serving engines, orthogonal to attention and compatible with continuous batching / fused prefill-decode. For our briefing it is a horizontal kernel-level sparse-inference observation, not a deployed at-scale system; the operationally meaningful number is the 1.34x end-to-end TPOT gain (and up to 25% extra sparsity at iso-quality), not the kernel-level 1.24-1.37x headline.
source_notes: The abstract headline '1.24x-1.37x average speedup (up to 2.51x)' corresponds to kernel-level spMspV measurements over SpInfer on A10G/L4 (Section 5.4, Figure 8); the end-to-end TPOT speedup is lower, averaging 1.34x (Section 5.5).
Artifacts at https://github.com/AIDASLab/SPDP; published as PVLDB 19(11) 2026.
Evidence pack covers abstract, intro, kernel profiling (Fig 8/9) and end-to-end eval (Fig 10/11); prefill kernel (Fig 12) and SuiteSparse (Fig 13) figures referenced but only qualitatively described.

Repair supplement (PDF Pages 5, 8) added the Section 3.2.3 roofline CI model, the Section 3.3 realization challenges (8x Tensor-Core CI drop under mma.m16n8k16), and the Section 4.2-4.3 kernel pipeline / prefill-SpMM design; it did NOT surface any energy/perf-per-watt data or Figure 12 prefill speedup numbers.

evidence_gaps.question: Does SPDP report a concrete performance-per-watt or energy measurement (watts/joules) backing the abstract's perf-per-watt claim, or is it only argued qualitatively?
What prefill-stage speedup does the Tensor-Core SpMM kernel achieve over cuBLAS and SpInfer (Figure 12 is referenced but no numbers given in the visible evidence)?
